title: Terraform against AWS: provider, state in S3 and locking in DynamoDB

videos.script: Terraform was taught against moto from the first day. Real accounts add three questions. {{three}} Whose credentials does Terraform act with? Never a key written in the file. A profile on a laptop, and a role in a pipeline. {{who}} Where does the state live, and who created that place? The bucket has to exist before the configuration that uses it. {{bucket}} And how is it locked? For years the answer was a DynamoDB table. Today it is a small file beside the state, and the table is deprecated. {{lock}} This lesson builds a state bucket that keeps every version and refuses to be public. Then it holds a lock and looks at it, in the table and in the bucket. And it moves from one lock to the other without a moment with no lock at all. {{move}} By the end, the record of everything Terraform manages sits somewhere safe, and two people cannot write it at once. {{end}}
